newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss seek ruling to hand Marcos fortune to Manila.
newsitem.headline: Swiss seek ruling to hand Marcos fortune to Manila.

text.p: Swiss justice officials on Thursday said they had asked the supreme court to make it easier to hand over to Philippine authorities a fortune left in Swiss banks by late dictator Ferdinand Marcos.

The motion filed with the Federal Court in Lausanne could be the final stage in over a decade of legal wrangling over whether some $500 million in Marcos' Swiss accounts should stay in Switzerland or be handed over to the Philippine government.

The Federal Bureau of Police Affairs, which represents the government in international legal matters, said it had asked the court to lift a key condition for repatriating the money to the Philippines for authorities there to decide on the ownership.
"If the Federal Court agrees to this, the assets could be entirely or partially handed over to Philippine authorities," the office said in a statement.

Specifically, the agency asked the court to drop its insistence in a 1990 ruling that the money only be returned once a Philippine court issued a binding sentence on the Marcos family and ordered the money confiscated, a step which has not yet been taken.
Marcos' widow Imelda was sentenced by a Manila court in 1993 to 18 years imprisonment for corruption but is free on bail pending appeals.

The Swiss police agency said the other parties in the row, led by the Marcos family on the one side and a group of Marcos torture victims on the other, had been notified of the government's action and would be able to file their own appeals against it if they wished.
An agency spokeswoman said it was up to the court to decide but added that the case in Switzerland could be closed for good if the court rules in favour of transferring the money.

"If we should win in court, then under normal circumstances the money would automatically be transferred to the Philippines...This could be the last stage (of the case) in Swiss courts," an agency spokeswoman told Reuters.
Separately, the Philippine government also appealed to the Federal Court, asking it to overturn a Zurich regional court ruling that the Marcos fortune remain frozen in Switzerland.

The Manila government lawyer in Switzerland, Martin Kurer, said he was challenging the Zurich court decision that upheld appeals by Marcos lawyers and Swiss banks against a 1995 decision to put the money into an escrow account in Manila.

The $500 million is part of what the Philippine government claims is some $5 billion looted from the economy by the Marcoses during their 20-year rule, before their overthrow in a 1986 popular revolt. The family denies stealing.
